executive_summary.question: What is the punishment for abetting the suicide of an ordinary person (not a child or person of unsound mind, delirium, or intoxication)?
executive_summary.generated_answer:
For abetting the suicide of an **ordinary person** (i.e., not a child, person of unsound mind, delirious person, or intoxicated person), the law prescribes:

- **Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years**, and  
- **Liability to fine**.  

This is set out in **Section 108** of the relevant provision [Chunk-ID: 13c9bef0-00e1-4778-ab87-e705bfe68f76].  

Additional procedural details (from the same enactment) indicate that the offence is **cognizable, non‑bailable, and triable by a Court of Session** [Chunk-ID: 91e1dfb3-35c8-4e65-bdd0-ed674d70420c].  

*Note:* If the person whose suicide is abetted falls under the special categories (child, unsound mind, delirious, or intoxicated), the punishment is more severe (death, life imprisonment, or up to ten years’ imprisonment plus fine) under Section 107 [Chunk-ID: 13c9bef0-00e1-4778-ab87-e705bfe68f76].
